title: Mara and the Parish
premise: Lena Pemberton, an insurance investigator with a photographic memory, is hired by a nervous parish treasurer named Elias Voss to prove that a murder has not yet happened — the predicted death of the parish's beloved vicar. When the vicar dies anyway, on schedule and in exactly the manner described, Lena realizes Voss didn't want prevention; he wanted a witness who could prove he wasn't there. Digging into the closed case of a chorister's drowning twelve years earlier, Lena uncovers a conspiracy of loyalty among the parish council that buried the truth to protect one of their own. In the end Lena must choose between exposing the found family that raised her late mother — and the truth she can never unknow — closing the case at cost of her own belonging.
about_author: Ivo Brightwater is the pen name of a former claims adjuster from coastal Maine who spent eleven years reading other people's disasters for a living. Their novels are known for quiet dread, meticulous detail, and protagonists who remember everything except how to let go.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Lena Pemberton's POV. A cash retainer arrives with no return address: prove that Vicar Aldous Crane will not be murdered before Easter. Lena, wary of hoaxes but haunted by three 'accidents' she quietly solved, takes the meeting. Emotional beat: professional skepticism masking a hunger for a puzzle worthy of her memory.

chapters.title: The Man Who Predicted It
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She traces the payment to Elias Voss, parish treasurer, who insists he received an anonymous letter naming the date and method of the vicar's death. He wants it disproven, not investigated. Beat: unease — Voss protests too precisely, and Lena's memory flags his rehearsed answers.

chapters.title: Stained Glass and Small Lies
chapters.summary: Lena attends Sunday service incognito, memorizing the congregation: the organist with shaking hands, the warden who watches doors, a young curate, Deenie, who seems terrified of the vicar. Beat: the warmth of parish community unsettles Lena, who never had one.

chapters.title: The Letter That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Voss shows Lena the threatening letter — then snatches it back, claiming he'll only surrender it to police. Lena reconstructs its exact wording from her single glance. Beat: frustration sharpening into certainty that Voss wrote it himself.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, archival research. The parish file mentions a chorister, Tom Ashby, drowned in 2012; ruled accidental. Lena's photographic recall matches details in old newsletters to inconsistencies in the coroner's report. Beat: the thrill of pattern recognition turning cold.

chapters.title: Deenie
chapters.summary: Deenie's POV. The curate remembers Tom Ashby — her childhood friend — and the night he died, which she was told to forget. She notices the new woman asking questions. Beat: guilt and tenderness; Deenie's loyalty to the parish wars with her grief.

chapters.title: Easter Eve
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. On the letter's predicted date, Lena stakes out the vicarage through a storm. At 11:40 p.m., the lights fail. Beat: rising dread, the sense of watching a clock she cannot stop.

chapters.title: Exactly As Described
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Vicar Crane is found dead at the foot of the bell tower stairs — the precise method from the letter. Police call it a fall. Lena, the only witness of the blackout, realizes she was meant to see nothing. Beat: horror braided with vindication.

chapters.title: The Witness Problem
chapters.summary: Detective Inspector Rourke's POV. Rourke, who once dismissed Lena's 'accident' theories, must now take her seriously. They form an uneasy alliance. Beat: grudging respect; Rourke warns Lena that parishes protect their own like families do.

chapters.title: What Voss Bought
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Reconstructing the timeline, Lena proves Voss's alibi is fabricated — he paid her to establish he feared a murder he was committing. But his terror seemed genuine. Beat: the first crack in her theory; someone else knew the plan.

chapters.title: The Choir Loft Key
chapters.summary: Deenie's POV. Deenie finds Tom Ashby's hidden diary behind the choir loft paneling and reads enough to be afraid: names, initials, a night at the reservoir. Beat: betrayal — the people who comforted her grief were its architects.

chapters.title: Everyone Swore It Was Closed
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The council closes ranks; the warden threatens Lena's license, the organist pleads with her to stop. Each denial gives her another memorized lie. Beat: isolation deepening — the found family theme inverted, a family built on silence.

chapters.title: Mother's Parish
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, flashback woven with present. Lena discovers her late mother grew up in this very congregation — and that Tom Ashby's diary mentions her maiden name. Beat: personal devastation; the case was always hers.

chapters.title: Rourke's Doubt
chapters.summary: Rourke's POV. Under pressure from above to close the vicar's death as accidental, Rourke secretly reopens the Ashby file and finds the original evidence bag logged empty. Beat: institutional rot; Rourke chooses truth over career.

chapters.title: The Reservoir Night
chapters.summary: Deenie's POV. Deenie finishes the diary: Tom saw the council's chairman, Marcus Hale, embezzle restoration funds; the 'accident' was punishment made example. Her mother helped cover it up. Beat: shattering of every comfort Deenie has leaned on.

chapters.title: A Trap Made of Memory
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Knowing Hale will move against anyone holding the diary, Lena lets word slip that it's in the vestry, then waits in the dark with perfect recall as her only weapon. Beat: controlled tension — Lena betting everything on being underestimated.

chapters.title: Hale
chapters.summary: Marcus Hale's POV. Hale comes for the diary, finds Lena, and speaks plainly: the parish survived because good people chose loyalty over truth, and so will she. Beat: chilling charisma; the antagonist almost persuades us.

chapters.title: The Bell Tower
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Hale corners Lena on the tower stairs where Crane died; Voss arrives, confessing he hired Lena hoping an outsider would expose what he couldn't. Struggle, sirens — Rourke heard the confession via Lena's open line. Beat: climax, fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Everything I Remember
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In the interview room, Lena recites twelve years of memorized lies verbatim — dates, denials, contradictions — until the council's story collapses under its own weight. Beat: catharsis; her curse becomes the instrument of justice.

chapters.title: Confessions at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Deenie's POV. Deenie reads Tom's diary aloud at a parish meeting rather than let it be buried again. Half the congregation weeps; half walks out. Beat: grief finally given language; the community breaking open to heal.

chapters.title: What the Parish Keeps
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Hale is charged; Voss, ruined but relieved, thanks her. Rourke offers Lena a consulting badge. Standing in the emptied church, Lena admits she came for a case and stayed for something like belonging. Beat: bittersweet resolution.

chapters.title: Mara and the Parish
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, epilogue. She learns 'Mara' was her mother's childhood nickname here — the title of a hymn page Tom Ashby kept. Lena pins it above her desk, closes the file, and opens a new envelope of unanswered questions. Beat: quiet hope; memory as inheritance, not burden.
